what: Batch 1009 group G3 (acceptance): the audited design (candidates K1, W1, I2, U1) and its audit, exported from the session scratchpad file items2/G3-acceptance.json, which the journal, the head-size record and the commit messages cite as the acceptance criteria. design.summary: Build all four, each smaller than proposed. U1 (the only structural change): one optional result key `unverified` on a done product-acceptance result, a list of {outcome, reason, check, owner, due_stage}. ShipLoop REFUSES only mechanical faults at the CLI gate (key missing, malformed entry, the unedited template row, due_stage not a later stage); it only RECORDS what it cannot judge (whether the list is complete, whether [] is true, assumption coverage, headline wording); it PRINTS the list and the plan's still-open assumptions at product-acceptance and handoff and renders it in report.html. No new state key; the key is shape-checked in _canonical_result (absence loads) and required only in a new submit-time gate, the assumptions pattern. Case end-state mapping: an `unverified` entry is the recorded 'unachievable / not yet due' state; 'validated another way' stays a script-run check. The shared CASE_END_STATES is left unchanged on purpose (its 'report blocked' route is wrong for an outer open item under S-14 and for the inner stages, which cannot continue past a failing recorded command); product-acceptance gets its own three-state sentence in DUTIES. I2: the Improve parent packet gets the stage's Goal and Done-when through _goal_lines (reviewer side) plus one sentence in _improve_line; no producer Checked-by change (head window). K1: one stage_files() union, two alias entries deleted. W1: five wording fixes (discovery no-suite, research/intake vs S-14, release guard scoped to plan review, integrate chain/commit lines, 'independent'); (f) is folded into U1. I built this in a scratch copy (/private/tmp/g3/proto2, a copy of the b1008a worktree at abc47622 plus the changes and patched tests; no repo file was edited). Result: all 60 ShipLoop hermetic test files pass except those that fail identically on a pristine copy (chain, chain-async, chain-lifecycle, chain-planning-context, cross-run: 23 failures on both; one status-display test) and one guidance test that needs docs/experiments, which my copy excluded. The seven patched test files fail on the pristine copy for the reasons listed in fail_first_tests. Measured head (dry run, END of the status block, limit 8000): product-acceptance 5973 to 6347, Improve parent packets 4529 to 4876 (inline) and 4758 to 5105 (ask-agent), every other stage within 2 characters; the step-plan head is untouched.
design.for_against: For: both runs ignored the stage row's own 'pending with its owner and due stage' and put an 'all verified' headline over a prose limitation (checkers results/nav-6e9289db headline 'live server meets every request sentence' with 'Limitation: ... not driven in a real browser'; battleship results/nav-c6fbc982 'all request outcomes verified; UI clicks only statically', notes/acceptance.md 'pending, optional, no authorized browser used'); S-14 has required a recorded open item since 2026-09-27 and the 2026-10-04 'a13' route (test/shiploop_e2e/LEARNINGS.md) was deliberately text-only with no field, so the content (owner, due stage, what they report) has nowhere to live; the gate is the same class as the plan's assumption list (required at submit, optional on load); the test blast radius is three helper defaults plus new cases. Against: a model can write [] or perfunctory text and the script cannot tell; n=2 on one model; product-acceptance was a pass-through stage (docs/lifecycle-review-2026-10-07.md: 0.4 min) and now needs one more field; it reverses the a13 'text only' choice for this one stage. Why smaller than the synthesis: no refusal keyed on prose, headline words or assumption ids (KISS over adversarial guards), no producer Checked-by edit (head window), no change to the owner's shared CASE_END_STATES, reportable-only items (script-run baseline, return-plan status, notes/ directory, refusal first lines) left to the other groups. The 5-field entry adds `check` to the synthesis's 4 because S-14's open item is 'who must do what and what they should report'; drop it if the second run shows it is filled perfunctorily.

per_candidate.change: Optional result key `unverified` ([{outcome, reason, check, owner, due_stage}], [] legal) on a done product-acceptance result. Submit-time gate refuses: key missing, entry not exactly those five non-empty texts, an entry equal to the printed template row, due_stage not one of release-plan, release-check, release, release-verify, operations, handoff. Records and prints: product-acceptance and handoff packets list the plan's assumptions still `open` (every consumer item is done by the outer stages); the handoff packet reprints the accepted list ('none listed' for [], 'no list recorded' when the key is absent: unmeasured is not zero); report.html gets an 'Unverified request outcomes' table with the same distinction. product-acceptance done_when[0] becomes 'every request outcome was observed by an executed check, or is listed in unverified with its reason, owner and due stage'; DUTIES['product-acceptance'] states the three end states (observed / observed another way, a changed method that ran / unachievable or not yet due, listed, run continues) and drops no existing text. Not built: refusal when open assumptions are unaccounted, headline parsing, script-updated assumption dispositions.

Reviewer side only: _goal_lines returns, for an active Improve child, 'Reviewing the accepted <stage> result. Goal: ...' and the row's done_when under 'Done when (the review confirms each; correct the result's files, never the condition):'. _goal_lines feeds both render and packet_head, so the printed head and the file carry it (one code path). Producer side: one added sentence after the unchanged promise in _improve_line ('That review checks the result against the Done-when conditions above.'), in the full packet after the status block, so no head growth. Not built: a Checked-by edit in the head (step-plan head is at the limit). Nuance the lens missed: the child's frozen exit condition already carries the done-when (improve_start_contract appends loop_contract.stage_exit; r1-checkers improve/nav-64cc858a.../terminal.json conditions.exit), so the runtime packets had it; the gap is the parent packet a cleared model re-reads (S-6), not a reviewer with no contract.

Wording only, one source each: (a) stage_spec discovery.done_when[0] adds 'or none exists and that is recorded as missing coverage'; (b) research.done_when[1] becomes 'each proven access need is recorded as an open item with who can grant it and the gate it blocks' and intake.done_when[1] 'who answers it (discovery, or a recorded default)'; (c) prompts._improve_prompt release_guard: for a stage in PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES (release-plan, the only release-family stage with an Improve child) say 'This review performs no deployment, MCP interaction or other release operation and repeats no release effect', keep the old 'may perform' text for the catalog's other release stages; (d) DUTIES['integrate']: 'confirm this item's candidate is assembled ... ShipLoop makes the item's commit when this stage is accepted' for both routes, and the bound-chain sentence moves into _INLINE_DUTY_PARAGRAPHS['integrate'] so inline runs never see it; (e) _BACKCHAIN_IMPROVE_OWNER: 'Improve is a broader review than Backchain's diagnostic'; (f) product-acceptance's missing end states is done in U1. Left alone: CASE_END_STATES vs the system-test open-item paragraph (owner's rule of today; documented below), the 7-refused-runs vs 'no iteration limit' pair (I1, document-only), the plan child's two-review vs one-pass pair.

Tables stay the only two; a close can no longer demand a file its packet does not name (test-spec gains {feature}/plan.md, release-plan gains {feature}/system-tests.md). risks: Saved runs: no new state key. `unverified` is a result key: _canonical_result accepts its absence, and _apply_result's replay compares canonical forms, so accepted product-acceptance results from older runs load and replay unchanged. A run that is mid product-acceptance when the plugin updates gets one refusal naming the exact shape (accepted).

Gaming and filler: [] or perfunctory text passes. Accepted and visible: the list is printed at handoff and in the report, and the second run is read for it. No prose or headline parsing is added (KISS over adversarial guards).

Dead-end refusal: the refusal names the key, the entry shape and the six legal due stages, and a test submits the corrected result through the same command. No path waits on a person (S-14) and an unachievable outcome continues the run.

Packet size and the window: product-acceptance +374 and Improve parents about +347 characters in the dry run, other heads within 2; step-plan head (7971 of 8000) not touched. Variable-length content (open assumptions, the handoff list) is placed after the status-block END, never in the kept head; a run with many open assumptions grows the packet file, not the head.

All were run in the prototype.

S-14 reading of the new refusal: it can block an unattended run only by refusing a malformed result; the model fixes it itself in the same stage, no person is involved.

corrections: U1 report: the design says html_section prints 'none listed' / 'not recorded' / the table. The prototype (/private/tmp/g3/proto2/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_unverified.py html_section) returns [] for both [] and an absent key. Either build the distinction or delete the claim. No test anywhere in proto2 asserts 'none listed' or 'no list recorded' at handoff (grep of proto2/test finds neither). Add a fail-first test for [] versus a result without the key, or the unmeasured-is-not-zero claim has no end state.

U1 open-assumption lines (shiploop_navigator._unverified_lines): the label 'Settled by: <row[check]>' prints the plan's 'what would settle it' text as if it were a fact. In both r1 runs most open assumptions were in fact settled by tests (checkers A2, battleship A2) but their disposition stays 'open' forever, and A3 (checkers) was not settled at all. Reword to 'Recorded open at planning (the ledger does not update dispositions) ... Check that would settle it: ...' and drop the 'still open although the work items are done' framing. Also remove the unstated limit=300 per-field truncation (bounded text also inserts a newline mid-bullet); print in full or use the existing default.

U1 due_stage is validated but never consumed. Only product-acceptance and handoff print the list, so an entry due at release-check, release, release-verify or operations is never shown to the stage that owns it. 'Not yet due' then has no route to one of the owner's end states. Smallest fix: let _unverified_lines also print the entries whose due_stage equals the current stage (one condition plus a test). Otherwise restrict due_stage to handoff and say that.

U1 canonical vs gate: _canonical_result runs on every accepted result at load (validate re-canonicalises). unverified.canonical currently enforces the exact five-key set and non-empty strings at load. The design itself says to drop `check` if it is filler; that later edit would refuse saved runs. Follow the skill_na comment in _canonical_result: canonical = list of mappings of strings only; exact FIELDS, non-empty text, template row and later-stage membership in check_submitted (CLI gate only).

U1 Checked-by line: _stage_gates names 'a missing unverified list, or an entry that is incomplete or still the template row' but not the fourth refusal, a due_stage that is not a later stage. The completeness test only pins the word 'unverified'. Name the due-stage fault (about +30 characters) so S-6 'how it is checked' is true.

U1 handoff wording: 'Unverified at product-acceptance: none listed' can be read by a cleared handoff model as 'nothing is open'. Open items recorded at system-test or release-verify in prose are not in it. Say explicitly that earlier and later stages' open items are read from their results, and keep 'none listed' scoped to product-acceptance.

I2 wording: 'Reviewing the accepted <stage> result' is false; the Improve parent packet itself says the parent step stays pending until improve-complete, so the result is not accepted. Use 'returned' or 'completed'. _improve_line says blocked and repeat results also start a child, and for those the 'Done when (the review confirms each ...)' block cannot hold. Condition the heading on child['seed_result']['outcome'] == 'done', or word it 'a done result must meet each'.

W1(d): drop the added sentence 'ShipLoop makes the item's commit when this stage is accepted'. The integrate row's Develop consideration already prints the same fact in the same packet (stage_spec integrate develop), which is duplication inside one packet. Keep only the removal of 'or commit' and the move of the bound-chain sentence into the delegated half of _INLINE_DUTY_PARAGRAPHS['integrate'].

W1(c): hold until the owner answers. test_improve_retains_coding_and_release_capabilities_with_stage_authority is a recorded owner decision. The existing text is already scoped to 'operations already authorized for the current task and stage', which at a plan review authorizes nothing. Both r1 release-plan Improve children ended on one trivial pass, so nothing broke. If the owner agrees, replace the guard outright. Do not keep the old text as an unreachable branch for release-check, release and release-verify, which never have an Improve child (reviewed only for the test's sake).

Delivery-contract minimal template (result_template over 6000 characters) omits `unverified` while the gate demands it, so a contract-mode run predictably gets one refusal at product-acceptance. Same class as the existing assumptions limit; accepted by the design.

A model can leave `reason`, `check` and `owner` as '<...>' placeholders and change only `outcome`: the refusal is exact equality with the whole template row, so a partly edited row passes. KISS may accept this; a one-line placeholder check (a value that starts with '<' and ends with '>') would close it, as the headline placeholder check does.

The +2 on the remaining stages is a path-length artifact (/private/tmp/g3/base versus /private/tmp/g3/proto2). All are far below 8000, so the conclusion stands but the evidence line is inexact.

Product-acceptance head growth is stated as 5973 to 6347 (+374). The same dry-run comparison gives about +414. Improve parents are stated as about +347; measured now: spec +443, plan +408, test-strategy +389, release-plan +364, system-test-author +268, and the carry-forward and other parents up to +591 (path artifact of +2 excluded).

'Real product-acceptance packets run about 720 characters longer than the dry run (r1-checkers nav-6e9289db END at 6695)'. 6695 is the offset of the narrative END marker. 'html_section prints none listed / not recorded / the table' and the report carries 'the same distinction': not what the prototype does (it prints nothing for [] or an absent key), and not tested.
'The Checked-by line names exactly what the gate refuses': it does not name the due_stage fault, one of the four refusals in unverified.check_submitted.

'Reviewing the accepted <stage> result' is not accurate: the Improve parent packet's own text says the parent step stays pending until improve-complete imports the review, so the seed result is not accepted yet.

The design says the open-assumption print lists the plan's assumptions 'still open'. The prototype's line pairs each with 'Settled by: <the plan's check>', which is the text of what would settle it, not a settling fact. Most of those assumptions were in fact settled by the consumer item's tests while their ledger disposition stays 'open', so the label asserts staleness as fact and misreads as a claim of settlement.

The fail-first entry that labels the text pins 'validated another way' misclassifies them (see corrections); and the design says the prototype 'built' items (SKILL.md paragraph, note, journal) that are not in /private/tmp/g3/proto2.
